title: ?? vs ||
explanation: || falls back on any falsy value, including 0 and ''. ?? only falls back on null or undefined. Use ?? for defaults where 0 is a real value.

title: Optional chaining
explanation: When ?. hits undefined, it skips the whole rest of the chain, so .name.first never runs. You don't need ?. at every step after the first one that might be missing.
hint: Once ?. finds nothing, does the rest of the chain still run?

title: Order around await
explanation: An async function runs synchronously until its first await. The rest is queued as a microtask, so the caller logs 3 before the function resumes and logs 2.
hint: How much of an async function runs before it gives control back to the caller?

title: Finding NaN
explanation: indexOf compares with ===, and NaN !== NaN. includes uses SameValueZero, which treats NaN as equal to itself.
hint: The two methods use different equality rules.

title: for...in on an array
code:
const arr = [10, 20];
for (const x in arr) console.log(x);
explanation: for...in loops over property keys, and keys are strings. It also includes inherited enumerable keys. Use for...of for values, or arr.entries() for both.

title: Promise.race vs Promise.any
explanation: race settles like the first promise to settle, so an early rejection wins. any resolves with the first fulfilled promise, ignoring rejections, and only rejects (with an AggregateError) if all of them reject. Use race for timeouts and any for "fastest mirror that works".
hint: One cares about the first promise to finish either way. The other only about the first success.

title: Closures
prompt: What is a closure? Give one practical use.
explanation: A function together with the variables that were in scope where it was created. It keeps them alive even after the outer function returns. Uses: private state (a counter only the returned function can change), memoization caches, and the timer variable inside debounce.
hint: What can an inner function still see after its outer function has returned?

title: Partial<T>
explanation: Partial is a mapped type that adds ? to every property. It's handy for update payloads: update(id, changes: Partial<User>). Its relatives are Required, Readonly, Pick and Omit.
hint: Think of a PATCH request that only sends the fields that changed.

title: Generic constraint
explanation: extends { length: number } means T must have a numeric length. Strings and arrays do. number doesn't, so the call fails to compile and never runs.

title: satisfies
prompt: What does satisfies do that a type annotation doesn't?
explanation: Both check the value against the type. An annotation (const x: T = …) then makes x exactly T, losing details. satisfies T keeps the narrower inferred type, so literal values and the exact keys of an object stay known.
hint: After the check, which one keeps the more specific inferred type?
